rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for units subject to the LA RSO are capped at the annual allowable percentage set by LAHD: 3% for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Beginning February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add any extra percentage increase for utilities. Landlords may pass through the RSO surcharge ($1.61/month) and the SCEP surcharge ($2.83/month) only after registering the units and giving written notice to the tenant.
rules.key_value: 3% annual allowable increase (7/1/2025-6/30/2026); no additional utility percentage from 2026-02-02
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles RSO (generally buildings with a certificate of occupancy on or before October 1, 1978); check ZIMAS for RSO status
rules.exemptions: Non-RSO properties are not subject to this cap (contact LAHD about allowable increases for non-RSO properties).
rules.interaction: Non-RSO units in Los Angeles may instead be subject to other limits (LAHD directs inquiries); state law separately requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1
rules.quoted_span: Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
rules.conflict_note: The page states the 3% figure applies July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, but the query date (2026-10-01) is after that period; the allowable percentage for July 1, 2026 onward is not stated on this page and may differ. Effective date reflects the 3% annual figure, not the original RSO enactment.
